note: Calm Tower content. Breathing is animation-timed (no visible numbers). Feelings route to a helper. Calm stories model naming feelings, taking space, asking for help; choices are shuffled and all get warm feedback. Body scan uses kid metaphors.

breathing.name: Bubble breath
breathing.line: Breathe in slowly and fill the bubble. Breathe out and let it float away.

breathing.name: Flower and candle
breathing.line: Smell the flower. Now blow out the candle, slow and long.

breathing.name: Unicorn breath
breathing.line: Breathe in like Luna before a big jump. Breathe out and land softly.

breathing.name: Starfish breath
breathing.line: Trace a finger up one side of your hand as you breathe in, down as you breathe out.

feelings.name: Happy
feelings.tip: Happy is wonderful. Let's keep it going with a story.

feelings.name: Sad
feelings.tip: It is okay to be sad. A calm story can help.

feelings.name: Angry
feelings.tip: Angry feels hot and big. Breathing makes it smaller.

feelings.name: Scared
feelings.tip: Scared is a signal. Let's squeeze and relax to feel safe.

feelings.name: Proud
feelings.tip: Proud! You did something hard. Luna is proud too.

feelings.name: Silly
feelings.tip: Silly is fun! Let's wiggle it out with a body scan.

feelings.name: Calm
feelings.tip: Calm and cozy. A bubble breath keeps it that way.

feelings.name: Tired
feelings.tip: Tired bodies need slow breaths and rest.

feelings.name: Worried
feelings.tip: Worries feel lighter when we say them out loud. Let's breathe first.

screens.text: Luna had a new class. Her tummy felt fluttery. "I feel nervous," she said.
Naming the feeling helped a little. Luna took three bubble breaths.

options.feedback: Asking for help is brave and smart.
Hiding is one way to feel safe. Asking for help works even better.
More breaths always help. Then she can ask for help too.

screens.text: Luna asked, "Can you show me where to sit?" The teacher smiled and helped. The flutters flew away.
Rosie built a tall tower. Crash! It fell down. Rosie felt hot and mad.
"I feel angry," Rosie said. That was the right name for it.

choice.prompt: What helps when you feel angry?

options.feedback: Taking space and breathing cools the hot feeling.
Throwing can hurt. Space and breathing work better.
Telling a grown-up is good. Breathing first helps too.

screens.text: Rosie sat on the soft rug and breathed. Then she built the tower again, even taller.
Sunny painted a sun. Minty said, "That looks weird." Sunny's face got hot.
Sunny felt hurt. Hurt is a real feeling. Sunny wanted to say so.

options.feedback: Saying how you feel is strong and kind.
Walking away is okay. Saying the feeling helps Minty understand.
Hurt words back make two hurt friends.

screens.text: Minty said, "I'm sorry. I like your sun." They painted a rainbow together.
It was bedtime. Luna's mind was full of worries. They buzzed like bees.
"I feel worried," Luna whispered. Saying it made the buzz a little quieter.

options.text: Squeeze and relax each part of her body
options.feedback: A body scan tells the body it is safe to rest.
Telling a grown-up is a great idea too.
Playing wakes the body up. Rest needs calm.

screens.text: Luna squeezed her toes, then let them go soft. Then her legs. Then her tummy. Soon she was asleep.

bodyScan.squeeze: Squeeze your toes tight, like squishing mud.
bodyScan.release: Now let go. Let your toes feel soft.

bodyScan.squeeze: Press your legs into the floor, strong like tree trunks.
bodyScan.release: Now let go. Let your legs feel heavy and calm.

bodyScan.squeeze: Pull your tummy in, like a turtle in its shell.
bodyScan.release: Now let go. Let your tummy be soft and round.

bodyScan.squeeze: Squeeze your hands, like squeezing a lemon.
bodyScan.release: Now let go. Let your fingers feel loose.

bodyScan.squeeze: Lift your shoulders up to your ears.

bodyScan.release: Now let go. Let your face feel smooth.
